description.narrative: The objective of the Urban Water Supply and Wastewater Project for Vietnam is to increase access to sustainable water services and environmental sanitation in selected urban areas in project provinces. There are two components to the project. The first component is investments and project implementation this component will be implemented by the participating provinces for investments in water supply and environmental sanitation. Works, goods, and consulting services for project preparation, implementation, investments, and technical assistance will be supported under this component; and the second component is technical assistance there are two parts for this component: institutional strengthening and project monitoring. The sub-component will be implemented by the Ministry of Construction (MOC) to develop the sector through the establishment of an information base on the access and quality of service and support project implementation; and Improving the Efficiency of Investments and Operations. The sub-component will be implemented by the Ministry of Planning and Investment (MPI) to develop policies on applying wastewater tariffs and on promoting the role of the private sector.
To increase access to sustainable water services and environmental sanitation in selected urban areas in the Project Provinces

title.narrative: Number of people in urban areas that have improved sanitation due to the project

comment.narrative: <p>The total number of beneficiaries of improved sanitation was underachieved, standing at 49 percent. This is mainly due to limited wastewater household connections implemented during the project. The results presented reflect achievements for original environmental sanitation up to December 2017 and achievement for Di An Wastewater sub-project by December 2019. Updated data on results Data source: Project Completion Report from MOC, August 2019.</p>

title.narrative: Number of people in urban areas that have improved sanitation due to the project

comment.narrative: This indicators refers to the peoples that would directly benefited from the improved wastewater service, i.e. they would be accounted only in case if their house connections were established. In addition to these peoples, there were many other peoples benefited from the improved service as their wastewater also was collected and treated, though not directly if the city still uses combined sewerage system.

Increase in the volume of water sold annually

comment.narrative:
<p>As per the Additional Financing Project Paper, May 2016,  the indicator on "Increase in the volume of water sold annually" was defined as an intermediate results. However, during the project implementation, the indicator was also included as a PDO indicator. The team tried to remove at completion, but it was no longer possible. As such, the results achieved for this indicator are presented both in the PDO indicator as well as in the intermediate indicator.</p>
<p>The volume of water sold was overachieved, reaching 127 percent by the December 2017. The results presented reflect achievements for original water supply sub-projects up to December 2017. Results achieved by December 2019 are not available. Data source: Project Completion Report from Ministry Construction, August 2019.</p>

title.narrative: New piped household water connections that are resulting from the project intervention

comment.narrative: This indicator has been overachieved due two reasons (i) new connections were directly increasing number of costumers of water utilities and so utilities have a motivation for making them, and (ii) connecting to piped water service would give direct benefits to households in improving their living conditions so they also have motivation for making them. The new connections counted should meet the design standards, i.e should have 24/7 service availability with water quality as regulated by the Government (Ministry of Health)

title.narrative: Increase in the satisfaction rate of beneficiaries

comment.narrative: The project-end survey was conducted by end of 2016 as it was planned. By that time, drainage/sanitation projects just completed construction and commission, thus many peoples didn't see the improvement and that leaded to negative results during the survey

title.narrative: Increase in the satisfaction rate of beneficiaries

comment.narrative: <p>The overall satisfaction rate of beneficiaries was slightly overachieved. The latest customer satisfaction rate was accessed on March 2020 for all subprojects, except for Di An wastewater and drainage subproject, which was carried in December 2019. The results reflected the aggregated customer satisfaction rate for water supply and environmental sanitation service provision. Data source: Binh Duong Completion Report, March 2020 and customer satisfaction survey conducted by the PPMU with support from the World Bank task team, on March 2020.</p>

The indicator includes beneficiaries from both water supply and drainage/sanitation services. While the number of beneficiaries of drainage/sanitation projects was a bit lower than the targeted, the number of beneficiaries of water supply projects has overachieved.

<p>By the project closing, the water security priority investments were not finalized. However, options for consideration have beenprepared and those include i) regional infrastructure to supply the affected areas or ii) provincial infrastructure to supply each affected area. The Ministry of Construction is currently assessing the options presented and feasibility studies and detailed designs will be conducted once the decision is made. Data source: Interview with the Ministry of Construction, March 2020.</p>
Some studies for this investment were prepared, but the main document - project FS - yet to be prepared.
